title: Guardrail evaluation + auto-stop/rollback triggers for route experiments (soft-stop first, hard-stop optional)
creator: Jada Williams
description:
Implement guardrail evaluation for route-level experiments and integrate with notifications + stop/rollback controls.

Scope (GA):
- Evaluate guardrails continuously for active experiments using standardized metrics: latency (p95/p99), error rate, cost/token.
- Soft-stop behavior (default): mark experiment as Degraded and notify (Console banner + Slack/oncall notification); do NOT automatically change traffic routing by default.
- Optional hard-stop (gated): allow auto-stop of experiment (set allocation to 0% for non-control variants or transition experiment to Stopped) when severe guardrail breach occurs; must include kill switch.
- Ensure guardrail evaluation is auditable and consistent with existing Rollouts semantics (fallback policies + canary rollouts).

Non-goals (this ticket):
- Statistical significance / full experiment analysis engine.
- Customer-defined custom metrics.

Why: Beta feedback + SRE requirements: customers need safe, predictable operations and quick detection of regressions without manual dashboard babysitting.
acceptance_criteria: Guardrail definitions are persisted in experiment config and validated server-side (required fields, sane thresholds, window).
Guardrail evaluator runs for active experiments and produces a deterministic, queryable status: Healthy | Degraded | Breached (or equivalent).
Soft-stop path: when breached, experiment status is updated and notifications are emitted (at minimum: audit event + internal notification hook + Console banner support).
Hard-stop path (optional): can be enabled per-account or per-experiment behind a feature flag; includes a global kill switch; emits audit event detailing trigger + metrics snapshot.
Alerting hooks exist for oncall (at least one canonical alert per guardrail type) and link to runbook.
No material increase in metrics cardinality or DB load beyond agreed thresholds; evaluator uses rollups/aggregates not raw spans.
End-to-end tests cover: guardrail breach detection, soft-stop status propagation to Console, and hard-stop behavior when enabled.
implementation_notes:
Design notes / decisions:
- Evaluation windows: start with 5m rolling window computed from the experiment rollup table (ENG-9027). Keep the evaluator window configurable but validated (min 1m, max 60m) to avoid both noisy flaps and slow detection.
- Baseline strategy (MVP): absolute thresholds only (e.g., p99 > X ms, error_rate > Y%). We explicitly defer relative deltas vs control until we have stable control-variant rollups and enough traffic.
- Guardrail status model:
  - Healthy: within thresholds.
  - Degraded: threshold exceeded but below “severe” level OR insufficient confidence (low sample) and warning configured.
  - Breached: severe threshold exceeded (used by hard-stop when enabled).
- Sample size gates: require minimum requests in the window before evaluating (per metric). If below min_requests, status remains Healthy with a “not enough data” note (Console copy handled elsewhere).
- Soft-stop semantics:
  - Does not change routing policy.
  - Writes guardrail_status + last_breach_at on the experiment.
  - Emits notification event with top offending metric + values + window.
- Hard-stop semantics (gated):
  - When enabled and Breached triggers, transition experiment to Stopping → Stopped (or equivalent) via the same state machine used by Console start/stop endpoints.
  - Stop action must be idempotent and safe under retries.
  - Include a global kill switch (config flag) requested by SRE after false-positive concerns.
- Precedence: guardrail-triggered stop should occur AFTER experiment assignment but BEFORE fallback/canary interactions cause confusing mixed routing. The stop action updates experiment allocation/config; router behavior follows normal config propagation rules.

Operational considerations:
- Avoid flapping: add a cooldown (e.g., 15m) between breach notifications per experiment + metric.
- Attribution integrity: if attribution drop rate is high, don’t hard-stop based solely on experiment metrics (could be blind). For MVP, treat attribution anomalies as separate alerts (ENG-9033) and block hard-stop unless attribution is above a floor.

test_plan:
Unit tests:
- Guardrail threshold evaluation for p95/p99/error_rate/cost_token with min_requests gate.
- Cooldown behavior for repeated breaches.
- Hard-stop gating (per-experiment + global kill switch).

Integration tests (staging):
- Generate synthetic traffic to a test route with two variants; inject latency regression on variant B; verify status transitions + notifications.
- Verify that stop action is idempotent under evaluator retries.
- Verify that stopping the experiment returns routing to non-experiment policy without requiring manual intervention.

Failure mode tests:
- Rollup lag: evaluator should mark status Unknown/Delayed (no stop) when rollup freshness exceeds threshold; emit internal warning event.
- Config propagation lag: stop event emitted but router still sees old config—ensure dashboards show propagation lag and do not repeatedly attempt stop.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Beta):
- Enable soft-stop only for allowlisted accounts behind feature flag route_experiments_guardrails.
- SRE to monitor alert noise + false positives; tune thresholds + windows.

Phase 2 (Late beta / pre-GA):
- Add optional hard-stop for p99 latency regressions only; gate behind route_experiments_hard_stop flag.
- Require kill switch route_experiments_hard_stop_kill_switch to be documented and owned by oncall.

GA:
- Soft-stop on by default.
- Hard-stop remains opt-in, requiring explicit enablement and SRE sign-off for enterprise accounts.
comments: 2025-02-07 (Rafael Mendes): Proposed initial guardrails: p99 latency, error_rate, cost/token. Avoid quality guardrails here; will hook evals in Applied ML workstream later. Agree on absolute thresholds only for MVP to reduce confusion.

2025-02-10 (Marissa Cole): PM note: Console needs clear UX copy—‘Degraded’ vs ‘Stopped’ must be unambiguous. Soft-stop should not surprise customers by changing traffic. Hard-stop must be explicitly opt-in in GA messaging.

2025-02-14 (Sean Gallagher): SRE review: add cooldown and require min sample size; otherwise alert noise will be unmanageable. Also require a kill switch for any automated stop behavior before broader beta.
2025-02-28 (Logan Wright): Telemetry dependency: rollup freshness metric is critical; evaluator should not act on stale data. Please consume the rollup watermark we’re adding in ENG-9027.

2025-03-05 (Chloe Martin): Console API state machine supports Stopping → Stopped; we can reuse it for evaluator-triggered stops but need to ensure audit event includes ‘trigger=guardrail’ and metrics snapshot.

2025-03-12 (Rafael Mendes): Soft-stop shipped behind flag; notifications wired to internal event bus + Console banner model. Hard-stop PR drafted but remains gated; waiting on final SRE thresholds and kill switch config plumbing.

2025-03-27 (Sean Gallagher): Approved enabling hard-stop in staging only for game day. Must link runbook in alert payloads and include escalation policy. Please ensure hard-stop does not loop if propagation lag delays stop taking effect.
2025-04-09 (Connor O'Brien): Marking Done for console-2025.04 release train. Hard-stop remains off by default; soft-stop + notifications on by default at GA.
